fullPassage:
Letters from Recent Graduates

Welcome to a new season of High School Magazine. To start off the new school year on the right foot, we asked some of our recent graduates to give us tips on how to succeed in the coming year and beyond.

Compare Apples to Apples
Nahyeon Kim Class of 2024

In high school, everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I dreamed of becoming an illustrator. In university, though, everyone seemed much more talented than me, and they all worked so hard that I felt small in comparison. I thought about giving up my dream of becoming an artist. Then one day, I happened to see a drawing I had won an award for from middle school on the kitchen wall. I was embarrassed because it wasn't very good.

People say you shouldn't compare apples to oranges, and they're right. That's why it doesn't make sense to compare yourself to Internet personalities or even people in your real life. Maybe they had an advantage, or even a disadvantage, that you didn't. If you are going to compare yourself to anyone, the only fair comparison is "yesterday-you." Only you know where you started and how much effort you've put in. I couldn't see the progress in my ability when I only compared myself to others. Everyone develops differently. I'm able to see now the drawing in the kitchen was full of mistakes that I no longer make. It is empowering to see how I have improved rather than to envy the success of others. Your competition isn't the person next door or the influencer on social media: it's you.

Don't Be Afraid to Speak Up
Elias Walter Class of 2025

Do you share your opinion in class discussions, or do you just stay silent and keep it to yourself? Like many of you, I often found myself in the second group. A little black hole inside of me swallowed my voice when I considered speaking up. The consequences of being ridiculed or being wrong were always on my mind.

Then, after a particularly heated conversation in class, I asked myself, "What am I afraid of?" I was scared that bad things would happen, but I never thought about good things. When I noticed others taking risks, I knew that I needed to do the same in order to participate. Many people are scared to speak up, but a lot of them do it anyway because they think it's worth it. So I left my comfort zone and started to speak up. I grew intellectually and socially by expressing myself more clearly. I got closer to friends who liked how open I was with them. Now I have more people with whom I can talk, share my ideas, and learn new things. Remember, taking the risk of expressing yourself can be extremely rewarding in unexpected ways.

Use Energy on What You Can Control
Abigail Princeton Class of 2022

As I worked through my second year into my third in college, I had more troubles balancing school and personal life. I would get excited, anxious, worried, and bored all at once and then separately. I would get exhausted when I had to write a report for my courses, mediate a disaster between friends, and respond to the comments on my online journal. I was drowning in a sea of responsibilities, concerns, and anxieties, and that was when I read an article with a simple insight.

The article advised me to draw two big circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my circle of influence, and I have direct control over the things inside it: what I eat and drink, how I behave, or what I do after school. The bigger circle is called my circle of concern: things I worry about but have no direct control over. For example, I have no direct control over how my professor will react to my report, but I do have control over the amount of research I do for it. Believing that everything was in my circle of influence left me stressed out and constantly exhausted. By wasting less energy on my circle of concern, I was able to invest more energy into things that mattered. I no longer worry about what my friends think, and I focus on my own actions. I don't get anxious over what might be on the test, and instead I put in every effort to understand the concepts themselves. Now, I only put my mental and physical energy into my circle of influence: eating healthy, staying in shape, and working hard.

questions.passage: In high school, everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I dreamed of ①<u>become</u> an illustrator. In university, though, everyone seemed much more ②<u>talented</u> than me, and they all worked so hard that I felt small in ③<u>comparison</u>. I thought about giving up my dream of becoming an ④<u>artist</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 나는 삽화가가 되는 것(becoming)을 꿈꿨다. become → becoming (전치사 of 뒤에 동명사)
det.analysis:
✅ ① become → becoming: dreamed of 뒤에 동명사(-ing) 필요. 전치사 of + 동명사
❌ ② talented: 비교급 more talented 정상
❌ ③ comparison: 전치사 in + 명사 정상
❌ ④ artist: 명사 정상
det.tip: 전치사(of/about/in) + 동명사(-ing). dream of becoming = ~이 되는 것을 꿈꾸다

questions.passage: A little black hole inside of me ①<u>swallowed</u> my voice when I ②<u>considered</u> speaking up. The consequences of ③<u>being ridiculed</u> or being wrong were always on my mind. Then, after a particularly ④<u>heating</u> conversation in class, I asked myself, 'What am I afraid of?'
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 특히 열띤(heated) 대화 후에 나는 스스로에게 물었다. heating → heated (감정을 유발하는 형용사)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ heating → heated: 대화가 '열띤' 상태이므로 과거분사 heated가 적합. heating은 '가열하는'이라는 물리적 의미
❌ ① swallowed: 과거형 정상
❌ ② considered: 과거형 정상
❌ ③ being ridiculed: 수동태 동명사 정상
det.tip: heated(열띤, 격렬한) vs heating(가열하는). heated argument/conversation = 열띤 논쟁/대화

questions.passage: I grew intellectually and socially by ①<u>expressing</u> myself more clearly. I got closer to friends ②<u>who</u> liked how open I was with them. Now I have more people with ③<u>whom</u> I can talk, share my ideas, and learn new things. Remember, taking the risk of expressing yourself can be extremely ④<u>reward</u> in unexpected ways.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 자신을 표현하는 위험을 감수하는 것은 극도로 보람 있을(rewarding) 수 있다. reward → rewarding (형용사 보어)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ reward → rewarding: be동사(can be) 뒤 보어 자리에 형용사 필요. reward(명사/동사)가 아닌 rewarding(형용사)
❌ ① expressing: 전치사 by + 동명사 정상
❌ ② who: 주격 관계대명사, 선행사 friends 수식 정상
❌ ③ whom: 전치사 with + 목적격 관계대명사 정상
det.tip: be + 형용사(보어). reward(n./v.) → rewarding(adj. 보람 있는). can be extremely rewarding

questions.passage: The article advised me ①<u>to draw</u> two big circles, with myself in the center. Believing that everything was in my circle of influence ②<u>left</u> me stressed out and constantly exhausted. By ③<u>wasting</u> less energy on my circle of concern, I was able to invest more energy into things that ④<u>matter</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 중요한 것들에 더 많은 에너지를 투자할 수 있었다. matter → mattered (과거 시제 일치)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ matter → mattered: 주절이 과거(was able to)이므로 관계절도 과거 시제 일치 필요
❌ ① to draw: advise + O + to V 정상
❌ ② left: 동명사 주어(Believing ~) + 과거동사 left 정상
❌ ③ wasting: 전치사 By + 동명사 정상
det.tip: 시제 일치: 주절 과거(was able to) → 종속절도 과거(mattered). things that mattered = 중요했던 것들

questions.passage: Do you share your opinion in class discussions, or do you just stay silent and keep it to yourself? Like many of you, I often found myself in the second group. A little black hole inside of me swallowed my voice when I considered speaking up. The consequences of being ridiculed or being wrong were always on my mind. So I left my __________ and started to speak up.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 나는 안전지대(comfort zone)를 떠나 말하기 시작했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② comfort zone: 원문 그대로. 두려움을 극복하고 익숙한 영역을 벗어난다는 의미
❌ ① social circle(사교 모임): 떠난 것은 사교 모임이 아님
❌ ③ study group(스터디 그룹): 문맥과 무관
❌ ④ waiting list(대기 명단): 문맥과 무관
det.tip: comfort zone = 안전지대, 편한 영역. leave one's comfort zone = 안전지대를 벗어나다

questions.passage: I'm able to see now the drawing in the kitchen was full of mistakes that I no longer make. It is ①<u>empowering</u> to see how I have improved rather than to ②<u>envy</u> the success of others. Your ③<u>competition</u> isn't the person next door or the ④<u>follower</u> on social media: it's you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 당신의 경쟁 상대는 옆집 사람이나 소셜 미디어의 인플루언서(influencer)가 아니다. follower(팔로워)는 influencer(인플루언서)와 반대 위치이므로 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ follower(팔로워) → influencer(인플루언서)가 원문. 비교 대상은 영향력 있는 사람이지 따르는 사람이 아님
❌ ① empowering(힘을 주는): 원문 그대로
❌ ② envy(부러워하다): 원문 그대로
❌ ③ competition(경쟁 상대): 원문 그대로
det.tip: influencer(영향력 있는 사람) ↔ follower(따르는 사람). 소셜 미디어에서 비교 대상 = influencer

questions.passage: In high school, everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I dreamed of becoming an illustrator. In university, though, everyone seemed much more talented than me, and they all worked so hard that I felt small in comparison.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"나현은 고등학교에서 재능 있는 예술가로 인정받았다."

det.korean: everyone told me how talented an artist I was = 모두가 내가 얼마나 재능 있는 예술가인지 말해줬다. 원문 일치.
det.analysis:
✅ T: 원문에 'everyone told me how talented an artist I was'라고 명시
❌ F: 원문과 정확히 일치하므로 F는 부적절
det.tip: how talented an artist I was = 감탄문의 간접화법. 재능 있는 예술가라는 평가를 받았다는 뜻

questions.passage: The article advised me to draw two big circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my circle of influence, and I have direct control over the things inside it. The bigger circle is called my circle of concern: things I worry about but have no direct control over.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"영향력의 원(circle of influence)이 관심의 원(circle of concern)보다 더 크다."

det.korean: 원문: The smaller circle is my circle of influence / The bigger circle is called my circle of concern. 영향력의 원이 '작은' 원이고, 관심의 원이 '큰' 원이다. '더 크다'는 불일치.
det.analysis:
✅ F: smaller circle = influence, bigger circle = concern. 진술은 반대로 서술
❌ T: 원문과 반대 내용
det.tip: smaller circle = influence (작은 원), bigger circle = concern (큰 원). 크기가 뒤바뀌었는지 확인

questions.passage: Many people are scared to speak up, but a lot of them do it anyway because they think it's worth it. So I left my comfort zone and started to speak up. I grew intellectually and socially by expressing myself more clearly.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"Elias는 많은 사람들이 두려워서 말하지 않는다고 생각하여, 자신도 계속 침묵을 지키기로 했다."

det.korean: 원문: 많은 사람들이 두려워하지만 그래도 한다(do it anyway). Elias도 comfort zone을 벗어나 말하기 시작했다. '침묵을 지키기로 했다'는 불일치.
det.analysis:
✅ F: 원문은 'left my comfort zone and started to speak up' = 말하기 시작함. 침묵을 지킨 것이 아님
❌ T: 원문과 반대 내용. Elias는 말하기 시작했음
det.tip: do it anyway = 그래도 한다. 두려워도 가치 있으니 실행한다는 문맥

questions.passage: People say you shouldn't compare apples to oranges, and they're right. That's why it doesn't make sense to compare yourself to Internet personalities or even people in your real life. Maybe they had an advantage, or even a disadvantage, that you didn't. If you are going to compare yourself to anyone, the only fair comparison is 'yesterday-you.' Only you know where you started and how much effort you've put in. I couldn't see the progress in my ability when I only __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 나 자신을 다른 사람과만 비교했을 때(compared myself to others) 내 능력의 발전을 볼 수 없었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ compared myself to others: 원문 그대로. 타인과의 비교가 성장을 못 보게 한다는 핵심 주장
❌ ① focused on my strengths: 강점 집중은 긍정적 행동
❌ ② practiced drawing: 연습은 발전에 도움이 되는 행동
❌ ④ listened to my teachers: 선생님 말을 듣는 것과 무관
det.tip: compare yourself to others = 자신을 타인과 비교하다. 이것이 성장을 보지 못하게 하는 원인

questions.passage: Believing that everything was in my circle of influence left me stressed out and constantly exhausted. By wasting less energy on my circle of concern, I was able to invest more energy into things that mattered. I no longer worry about what my friends think, and I focus on my own actions. I don't get anxious over what might be on the test, and instead I put in every effort to understand the concepts themselves. Now, I only put my mental and physical energy into __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이제 나는 정신적, 신체적 에너지를 영향력의 원(my circle of influence)에만 투입한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① my circle of influence: 원문 그대로. 통제 가능한 것에만 에너지를 집중
❌ ② my circle of concern: 관심의 원은 에너지 낭비 영역
❌ ③ other people's opinions: 다른 사람 의견 걱정을 그만뒀다는 문맥
❌ ④ unpredictable outcomes: 예측 불가한 결과는 통제 불가 영역
det.tip: circle of influence = 통제 가능 영역 (식사, 행동, 노력). 글의 결론 = 통제 가능한 것에만 집중

questions.passage: Do you share your opinion in class discussions, or do you just stay silent and keep it to yourself? Like many of you, I often found myself in the second group. A little black hole inside of me swallowed my voice when I considered speaking up. The consequences of being ridiculed or being wrong were always on my mind.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: Elias는 항상 수업 토론에서 적극적으로 발언했다.
Elias는 친구들이 자신의 의견을 항상 지지해 주었다.
Elias는 블랙홀에 대한 과학 보고서를 작성했다.

det.korean: 조롱당하거나 틀리는 것의 결과가 항상 마음에 있었다 = 걱정했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 조롱/틀릴까 걱정: 'consequences of being ridiculed or being wrong were always on my mind' 원문 일치
❌ ① 적극적 발언: 'the second group'(침묵 그룹)에 속함
❌ ③ 친구들 지지: 언급 없음
❌ ④ 블랙홀 보고서: black hole은 비유적 표현
det.tip: a little black hole = 내면의 두려움을 비유. 과학적 블랙홀이 아님. 비유적 표현에 주의

questions.passage: As I worked through my second year into my third in college, I had more troubles balancing school and personal life. I would get exhausted when I had to write a report for my courses, mediate a disaster between friends, and respond to the comments on my online journal. I was drowning in a sea of responsibilities, concerns, and anxieties, and that was when I read an article with a simple insight.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: Abigail은 대학교 2학년에서 3학년으로 넘어갈 때 어려움을 겪었다.
그녀는 수업 보고서를 써야 할 때 지쳤다.
그녀는 온라인 일기의 댓글에 답해야 했다.

det.korean: 원문: 기사를 읽고 통찰을 얻었다(read an article with a simple insight). 친구의 도움이 아님.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 친구의 도움: 원문은 기사(article)를 읽고 깨달음을 얻음. 친구 도움은 언급 없음
❌ ① 2→3학년 어려움: 'second year into my third' 원문 일치
❌ ② 보고서 작성 피곤: 'write a report' 원문 일치
❌ ③ 온라인 일기 댓글: 'respond to comments on my online journal' 원문 일치
det.tip: an article with a simple insight = 간단한 통찰이 담긴 기사. 해결책은 친구가 아니라 기사에서 얻음

questions.passage: People say you shouldn't compare apples to oranges, and they're right. That's why it doesn't make sense to compare yourself to Internet personalities or even people in your real life. Maybe they had an advantage, or even a disadvantage, that you didn't. If you are going to compare yourself to anyone, the only fair comparison is 'yesterday-you.' Only you know where you started and how much effort you've put in. I couldn't see the progress in my ability when I only compared myself to others. Everyone develops different.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 찾아 바르게 고치시오.
ch: the only fair → the only fairly
where you started → where did you start

det.korean: 모든 사람은 다르게(differently) 발전한다. different(형용사) → differently(부사)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ different → differently: develops(동사)를 수식하므로 부사 differently가 필요
❌ ① shouldn't comparing: 조동사 뒤 동사원형 정상
❌ ② the only fairly: fair는 comparison을 수식하는 형용사로 정상
❌ ④ where did you start: 간접의문문은 S+V 어순 정상
det.tip: 동사 수식 = 부사. develops differently(다르게 발전한다). different(형용사)는 명사 수식

questions.passage: Then one day, I happened to see a drawing I had won an award for from middle school on the kitchen wall. I was embarrassed because it wasn't very good.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 찾아 쓰시오.

"나현은 중학교 때 상을 받았던 그림이 별로 좋지 않아서 __________(을/를) 느꼈다."

det.korean: 그림이 좋지 않아서 부끄러움(embarrassed)을 느꼈다.
det.analysis: 원문 'I was embarrassed because it wasn't very good'에서 embarrassed를 찾아 쓰는 문제.
det.tip: embarrassed = 부끄러운, 창피한. be embarrassed = 부끄러움을 느끼다

questions.passage: The smaller circle is my circle of influence, and I have direct control over the things inside it: what I eat and drink, how I behave, or what I do after school. The bigger circle is called my circle of concern: things I worry about but have no direct control over.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 찾아 쓰시오.

"더 큰 원은 내 __________의 원이라 불리며, 걱정은 하지만 직접적인 통제권이 없는 것들이다."

det.korean: 더 큰 원은 나의 관심(concern)의 원이라 불린다.
det.analysis: 원문 'The bigger circle is called my circle of concern'에서 concern을 찾아 쓰는 문제.
det.tip: circle of concern = 관심/걱정의 원. concern = 걱정, 관심사

questions.passage: People say you shouldn't compare apples to oranges, and they're right. __________. Maybe they had an advantage, or even a disadvantage, that you didn't.

det.korean: 자신을 인터넷 유명인과 비교하는 것은 의미가 없다.
det.analysis: it(가주어) + doesn't make sense + to V(진주어): ~하는 것은 의미가 없다.
det.tip: It doesn't make sense to V = ~하는 것은 말이 안 된다/의미가 없다. 가주어 it + 진주어 to V 구문

questions.passage: People say you shouldn't compare apples to oranges, and they're right. That's why it doesn't make sense to compare yourself to Internet personalities or even people in your real life. Maybe they had an advantage, or even a disadvantage, that you didn't. If you are going to compare yourself to anyone, the only fair comparison is 'yesterday-you.' Only you know where you started and how much effort you've put in. I couldn't see the progress in my ability when I only compared myself to others. Everyone develops differently.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 다른 사람과 경쟁해야 더 빨리 성장할 수 있다.
인터넷 유명인을 롤모델로 삼는 것이 중요하다.
자신을 타인이 아닌 과거의 자신과 비교해야 한다.
예술가가 되려면 대학 교육이 반드시 필요하다.

det.korean: 자신을 비교하려면 유일하게 공정한 비교 대상은 '어제의 나'이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 과거의 자신과 비교: 'the only fair comparison is yesterday-you'
❌ ① 경쟁으로 성장: 타인 비교를 하지 말라는 내용
❌ ② 롤모델: Internet personalities를 비교 대상에서 제외
❌ ④ 대학 교육: 교육 필요성은 주제가 아님
det.tip: 핵심: compare yourself to 'yesterday-you' = 자기 자신의 성장에 초점

questions.passage: The article advised me to draw two big circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my circle of influence, and I have direct control over the things inside it. The bigger circle is called my circle of concern: things I worry about but have no direct control over. By wasting less energy on my circle of concern, I was able to invest more energy into things that mattered. Now, I only put my mental and physical energy into my circle of influence: eating healthy, staying in shape, and working hard.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 걱정이 많을수록 더 열심히 노력하게 된다.
친구 관계가 대학 생활의 가장 중요한 부분이다.
통제할 수 있는 것에 에너지를 집중해야 한다.

det.korean: 관심의 원에 에너지를 낭비하지 말고, 통제할 수 있는 것(영향력의 원)에 에너지를 집중하라.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 통제 가능한 것에 집중: circle of influence에 에너지를 투입하라는 핵심 메시지
❌ ① 건강한 식습관: 예시 중 하나일 뿐 핵심 주제 아님
❌ ② 걱정이 동기부여: 걱정(concern)에 에너지를 낭비하지 말라는 반대 메시지
❌ ③ 친구 관계: 주제가 아님
det.tip: circle of influence(통제 가능) vs circle of concern(통제 불가). 핵심: 통제 가능한 곳에 에너지 집중

questions.passage: Then, after a particularly heated conversation in class, I asked myself, 'What am I afraid of?' I was scared that bad things would happen, but I never thought about good things. When I noticed others taking risks, I knew that I needed to do the same in order to participate.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 찾아 쓰시오.

"다른 사람들이 위험을 감수하는 것을 알아차렸을 때, Elias는 참여하기 위해 __________(을/를) 해야 한다는 것을 알았다."

det.korean: 나도 참여하기 위해 같은 것(the same)을 해야 한다고 알았다.
det.analysis: 원문 'I knew that I needed to do the same in order to participate'에서 the same을 찾아 쓰는 문제.
det.tip: do the same = 같은 것을 하다 (= 위험을 감수하다). in order to = ~하기 위해
